title: A truerhearted lass never drew the breath of life, always with a laugh in her gipsylike eyes and a frolicsome word on her cherryripe red lips, a girl lovable in the extreme.
html_source:
Joyce brings the romantic clichés to an extreme, and imbues the description with something beyond the clichés they expose – instead of being a mockery of the cliché and therefore a mockery of the characters, the language itself is shown to be hollow but the characters manoeuvre within it, push outside of it, and become real characters in their own right. Contrast with the use of clichés in Beckett’s Murphy where clichés are rolled out to sneer at the characters and their petty foibles.

This is typical of Joyce’s appropriation of language, cant, phrases and clichés.
